reasons: No tests are visible for this file.
It imports from scan-template while scan-template imports from it, a circular import.
Some values are used with non-null assertions, so missing data would produce wrong text rather than a clear error.

terms.meaning: A pointer that says where a number or sentence came from.
A date worked out from the planned end plus the delay, not a recorded completion date.
Two files that each load the other, which can leave one of them incomplete when it is first used.
The summary findings section of the deck, shown in a comparison layout.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for review rules
sections.what: Brings in the types and helper functions this file needs: citation types, the chart project filter, and the capital cost and capacity lookups from the template file.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: This file imports from the template file, and the template file imports from here. Changing either import can break loading.

sections.name: reviewRef
sections.title: Finding the citation for a field
sections.what: Returns the citation for one project field. If the project has none under that name, it tries an older name used by earlier saved decks. If nothing matches, it returns a bare reference that names only the project and field, with no quote or link.
sections.why: The comment says references stay specific to the field, so a reader can still see which field a number came from even without a quote.
sections.watch_out: A bare reference looks like a citation but proves nothing. Check the quote or link before trusting the number.

sections.name: scheduleEndDisplay
sections.title: Schedule end date text
sections.what: Chooses what the schedule end shows for a project. A recorded actual end is shown as is. Otherwise a calculated end is shown, marked as implied, using the planned end plus the delay in months. If neither exists, the text says not recorded.
sections.why: The comment states that a calculated date is not a real outcome, so the calculation and its formula are attached to the text.
sections.watch_out: The implied date is only as good as the planned end and delay values. A wrong delay gives a confident-looking date.

sections.name: numericalSynthesis
sections.title: Automatic numeric findings
sections.what: Writes the findings for the synthesis slides straight from the numbers. It lists up to three projects with the largest cost deviations, up to three with the largest schedule overruns, and up to three with the largest portfolio budgets. Each line includes the citation for its inputs and avoids naming causes.
sections.why: The comment says these findings are deterministic, so they never invent causes or claim that something was not reported.
sections.watch_out: The sorting assumes that every project passed in already has its percentage values. The chart filter is expected to remove incomplete projects first, or the text will be wrong rather than failing clearly.

summary: Decides what schedule end date a project shows and writes the automatic numeric findings for the summary slides, always keeping track of where each number came from.
purpose: Holds the rules for showing a finish date, including the difference between a real completion date and a calculated one, and the rules for writing findings from the numbers.
why: Comments say findings must not invent causes or claim that something was not reported. A calculated date is kept separate from a real completion date.
how: First, it finds the citation for a field, trying an older field name if the newer one is missing. Second, for the end date, it uses the recorded actual end if there is one, otherwise it calculates an implied end from the planned end plus the delay, otherwise it says the date is not recorded. Third, for findings, it ranks delivery projects by cost and by schedule overrun, ranks all projects by budget, and writes up to three lines for each ranking with citations.
inputs: A project record, a field name, or a list of project records.
outputs: Citation objects, a date text with its citation, and lists of finding bullets for the synthesis slides.
risks: The implied end date is a calculation, not a verified fact. The findings ranking uses values that are assumed to be present. This file and scan-template import from each other, which can cause errors if one is changed carelessly.
debug: If a date looks wrong, check the planned end and delay values in the saved project. If a citation is missing, check the sources record and the older field names. If a findings list is empty, check that projects have both percentage values.
